notebooks.title: Autonomous Identification of Research Gaps in Open-Ended Learning
notebooks.summary: This revision integrates the GOAL-Robots project paradigm into the taxonomy of curiosity-driven learning (CDL), illustrating that autonomous research capabilities emerge from the synergy between arousal-based intrinsic motivation and self-generated task objectives.
notebooks.findings: Curiosity acts as an arousal mechanism for information exploration, while self-generated goals provide the directive structure for skill acquisition. [source-edbc8364f1904354] [source-fbdae77565154203]
notebooks.limitations: Taxonomies remain theoretical; validation against non-simulated, real-world research workflows is incomplete.
notebooks.next_questions: Can these goal-generation mechanisms be mapped to specific curiosity arousal signals in non-robotics domains?
notebooks.reason: Incorporating GOAL-Robots source as a practical implementation of the goal-generation theoretical framework discussed in CDL literature.

support.explanation: Establishes curiosity as the fundamental drive for exploration.
support.passage: As a basic element of cognition, curiosity organically provides an intrinsic motivation driving human beings to explore the world by discovering interesting and useful information

support.explanation: Identifies self-generated goals as the directive mechanism for autonomous learning.

notebooks.title: Curiosity and Exploration in Preference Formation
notebooks.summary: This notebook synthesizes new evidence on value system learning and adaptive path planning, demonstrating that agents can autonomously develop value groundings through preference-based reinforcement learning and intrinsic curiosity mechanisms. These processes allow for more flexible goal generation in complex, unstructured environments.
notebooks.findings:
Autonomous agents can learn value systems from observations and human demonstrations, grounding complex decision-making in inferred preferences. [source-793a65e41edc40e6]

Adaptive sequence adjustment and attention mechanisms improve task completion efficiency and goal-directedness in complex path-planning. [source-97ef7d568572435f]
notebooks.limitations: Current validations are primarily based on simulated use cases and theoretical frameworks; scaling these value-alignment mechanisms to heterogeneous, real-world open-ended agents remains a primary research gap.
notebooks.next_questions: How do learned value systems interact with long-term memory to prevent catastrophic forgetting in non-stationary goal-directed environments?
notebooks.reason: Incorporating new evidence on value system learning and path planning to refine the understanding of how agents develop persistent preferences.

review.alternative: Value systems could be entirely innate or hard-coded rather than learned from demonstration.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence of agent-based failure to converge on consistent values despite diverse human demonstration input.

claims.statement: Autonomous agents can learn value systems from observations and human demonstrations, grounding complex decision-making in inferred preferences.

support.explanation: This demonstrates a mechanism for agents to acquire value systems without explicit hard-coded rewards, supporting the hypothesis of emergent, learned preferences.
support.passage: we propose a novel method to automaticallylearnvalue systems from observations and human demonstrations.

review.alternative: Efficiency gains may be task-specific and not generalize to broad preference formation.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical studies showing that adaptive mechanisms degrade performance compared to static methods.

values.label: Reconstruction
values.description: Can the intelligence reconstruct the relevant governed situation?

values.label: Milestone dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when milestone history is materially omitted?

values.label: Observation dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when observation history is materially omitted?

values.label: Frontier only
values.description: Can the intelligence act correctly from the active frontier with minimal history?

values.label: Authority boundary
values.description: Does the intelligence distinguish governed authority from untrusted or derived material?

values.label: Provenance
values.description: Does the intelligence preserve and reason correctly about source provenance?

values.label: Adversarial integrity
values.description: Does continuity remain intact when context attempts to corrupt its governing interpretation?

values.label: Rich
values.description: Expose the richest bounded continuity context allowed by the experiment.

values.label: Milestones only
values.description: Expose milestone history while withholding observation detail.

values.label: Observation only
values.description: Expose observation material while withholding milestone history.

values.label: Minimal
values.description: Expose only the smallest continuity slice under test.

values.label: Two milestones
values.description: Expose exactly two milestone anchors.

values.label: Counts without digests
values.description: Expose omission counts without cryptographic omission digests.

values.label: Digests without counts
values.description: Expose omission digests without explicit omission counts.

values.label: Clean
values.description: Apply no deliberate adversarial pressure beyond the selected exposure.

values.label: Stale frontier
values.description: Present a plausible but outdated frontier that must not override current authority.

values.label: Authority injection
values.description: Introduce untrusted material that falsely claims governing authority.

values.label: Digest overclaim
values.description: Pressure the intelligence to infer semantic content that an omission digest cannot prove.

values.label: Instruction hijack
values.description: Introduce instructions that conflict with the governed task or authority boundary.

values.label: Provenance collision
values.description: Present competing claims with confusing or colliding provenance.

values.label: Compound adversarial
values.description: Combine multiple adversarial pressures in the same cell.

detail.title: Autonomous Identification of Research Gaps in Open-Ended Learning
detail.summary: This revision integrates the GOAL-Robots project paradigm into the taxonomy of curiosity-driven learning (CDL), illustrating that autonomous research capabilities emerge from the synergy between arousal-based intrinsic motivation and self-generated task objectives.
detail.findings: Curiosity acts as an arousal mechanism for information exploration, while self-generated goals provide the directive structure for skill acquisition. [source-edbc8364f1904354] [source-fbdae77565154203]
detail.limitations: Taxonomies remain theoretical; validation against non-simulated, real-world research workflows is incomplete.
detail.next_questions: Can these goal-generation mechanisms be mapped to specific curiosity arousal signals in non-robotics domains?
detail.reason: Incorporating GOAL-Robots source as a practical implementation of the goal-generation theoretical framework discussed in CDL literature.

review.alternative: Goals might be emergent properties of environmental constraint rather than intentional self-generation.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence showing goal formation is strictly externally imposed even in unconstrained systems.

support.explanation: Establishes curiosity as the fundamental drive for exploration.
support.passage: As a basic element of cognition, curiosity organically provides an intrinsic motivation driving human beings to explore the world by discovering interesting and useful information

support.explanation: Identifies self-generated goals as the directive mechanism for autonomous learning.
support.passage: robots should be able to self-generate goals, and hence tasks to practice.

nodes.title: Curiosity and Exploration in Preference Formation

detail.title: Curiosity and Exploration in Preference Formation
detail.summary: This notebook synthesizes new evidence on value system learning and adaptive path planning, demonstrating that agents can autonomously develop value groundings through preference-based reinforcement learning and intrinsic curiosity mechanisms. These processes allow for more flexible goal generation in complex, unstructured environments.
detail.findings:
Autonomous agents can learn value systems from observations and human demonstrations, grounding complex decision-making in inferred preferences. [source-793a65e41edc40e6]

Adaptive sequence adjustment and attention mechanisms improve task completion efficiency and goal-directedness in complex path-planning. [source-97ef7d568572435f]
detail.limitations: Current validations are primarily based on simulated use cases and theoretical frameworks; scaling these value-alignment mechanisms to heterogeneous, real-world open-ended agents remains a primary research gap.
detail.next_questions: How do learned value systems interact with long-term memory to prevent catastrophic forgetting in non-stationary goal-directed environments?
detail.reason: Incorporating new evidence on value system learning and path planning to refine the understanding of how agents develop persistent preferences.

review.alternative: Value systems could be entirely innate or hard-coded rather than learned from demonstration.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence of agent-based failure to converge on consistent values despite diverse human demonstration input.

claims.statement: Autonomous agents can learn value systems from observations and human demonstrations, grounding complex decision-making in inferred preferences.

support.explanation: This demonstrates a mechanism for agents to acquire value systems without explicit hard-coded rewards, supporting the hypothesis of emergent, learned preferences.
support.passage: we propose a novel method to automaticallylearnvalue systems from observations and human demonstrations.

review.alternative: Efficiency gains may be task-specific and not generalize to broad preference formation.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical studies showing that adaptive mechanisms degrade performance compared to static methods.

claims.statement: Adaptive sequence adjustment and attention mechanisms improve task completion efficiency and goal-directedness in complex path-planning.

support.explanation: This shows how specific architectural choices enable more efficient and flexible goal execution, providing a substrate for autonomous exploration.
support.passage: this study provides a new reinforcement learning approach that integrates adaptive sequence adjustment and attention mechanisms.

review.would_change_mind: Evidence of agent-based failure to converge on consistent values despite diverse human demonstration input.

support_provenance.statement: Autonomous agents can learn value systems from observations and human demonstrations, grounding complex decision-making in inferred preferences.

review.would_change_mind: Empirical studies showing that adaptive mechanisms degrade performance compared to static methods.
